lastText: OGSHARP RAPORUHome19141915191619171918HARD MODE — EROSION 3/430 October 1918The Armistice on LemnosThe armistice is signed in the harbour of Mudros on 30 October, aboard a British battleship, by the delegation of an empire whose armies have been beaten on every front it has fought on. The Straits are open to the Allies, the army is to go home and the garrisons in Arabia, Syria and Mesopotamia are to surrender. The war that the empire entered at the order of one minister and one German admiral ends with the empire's capital under Allied guns, and with a population that was told, for four years, that it was winning.The front · 30 October 1918Expand the mapSarikamisthe Suez CanalConstantinopleDamascusBeershebaBaghdadGazaAleppoNablusNazarethMudros-10MANPOWER ▾-10MUNITIONS ▾-10IMPERIAL CONTROL ▾Settled recordThe German ships, August 1914: admitted to the Straits and taken into the navy. Entering the war, 1914: the Black Sea raid, and war with Russia. Sarikamis, December 1914: the Erzurum line held through the winter. The Suez Canal, February 1915: a small column sent to raid the canal. Gallipoli, April 1915: the divisions placed above the beaches. Kut, winter of 1915-16: the siege broken by the relief force. Erzurum, 1916: the fortress held until it fell. The Hejaz, 1916: Medina held to the end of the war. Sinai, 1916: the attack at Romani. Baghdad, 1917: the line of the Diyala.
